s1.syndrome_frame: Hyperlipidemia with variable response to treatment and potential issues with laboratory measurements
salient_findings: Discrepancy between direct and calculated LDL-C measurements
History of adverse effects from statins
key_facts: Patient is a 47-year-old African American man
Medical history includes hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and gastroesophageal reflux disease
Patient has been tried on various statins
Patient experienced hip pain and elevated liver enzymes while on statins
Fasting lipid profile showed LDL-C of 232 mg/dL off lipid-lowering agents
Direct LDL-C was 113 mg/dL in June 2014
Direct LDL-C was 115 mg/dL in October 2015
Calculated LDL-C was 170 mg/dL in December 2015
Apolipoprotein B and Lipoprotein (a) measurements were performed

shortlist.label: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated LDL-C levels and variable response to statins

shortlist.label: Familial Defective Apolipoprotein B
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated LDL-C levels and potential issues with Apo B measurements

shortlist.label: Lipoprotein(a) Hyperlipoproteinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Lp(a) measurements were performed and may be relevant to patient's hyperlipidemia

shortlist.label: Familial Combined Hyperlipidemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's lipid profile and medical history suggest a possible familial component

shortlist.label: Polygenic Hypercholesterolemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's elevated LDL-C levels and response to statins suggest a possible polygenic cause

raw.rationale: The patient's significantly elevated LDL-C levels off lipid-lowering agents, along with the marked difference between direct and calculated LDL-C levels, suggests a problem with LDL receptor binding, which is consistent with Familial Defective Apolipoprotein B.

rejected.label: Familial Hypercholesterolemia
rejected.why: While the patient has high LDL-C, the response to statins (although limited by side effects) and the variability in LDL-C measurements do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lipoprotein(a) Hyperlipoproteinemia
rejected.why: There is no specific indication that elevated Lipoprotein(a) is the primary cause of the patient's hypercholesterolemia, as measurements were performed but not highlighted as abnormal.

rejected.label: Familial Combined Hyperlipidemia
rejected.why: This condition typically involves elevations in both LDL-C and triglycerides, but the vignette primarily focuses on LDL-C elevations without emphasizing triglyceride levels.

rejected.label: Polygenic Hypercholesterolemia
rejected.why: While possible, the significant elevation in LDL-C and the specific pattern of response to statins suggest a more specific defect in lipid metabolism, such as Familial Defective Apolipoprotein B.
